_README: Thresholds for segment_way_match.py, kept as data rather than module
constants so that each one can carry the measurement it came from.
A null value means 'not yet decided by measurement' and the code must
refuse to use it rather than fall back to a guess.
Follows the precedent set by src/road_access_rules.json.

vertex_cell_decimals.by: definition: latitude and longitude rounded to 6 decimal degrees count as identical

note: Rounding to a 6dp grid is a QUANTIZATION, not a tolerance: two points
1e-7 deg apart straddle a cell boundary and land in different cells, so
plain cell equality is brittle and NON-MONOTONIC in the number of
decimals (7dp scored better than 6dp). Checking the 3x3 cell
neighbourhood restores the intended semantics.
Measured on 203 ADB segments lying wholly inside a Bangkok bbox,
7,355 vertices, against the rebuilt OSM layer:
6dp exact cell          79.14% of vertices, per-segment median 0.850
6dp + 3x3 neighbourhood 87.56% of vertices, per-segment median 0.948
true distance <= 0.11 m 87.48% of vertices, per-segment median 0.944
The neighbourhood reproduces the distance test to within 0.08 points
and recovers the 8.4 points plain rounding loses.

bearing_tolerance_deg.by: the same 30-degree bearing test as tomtom_match_rules.json bearing_tolerance_deg, confirmed by measurement
note: Confirmed on the same sample: bearing difference to the nearest way is
median 0.6 deg, p90 3.9, p95 7.2 -- the nearest way almost always runs
the same way. The share beyond 30 deg SATURATES at 2.0% however far the
distance threshold is opened (1 m: 0.5%, 5 m: 1.7%, 20 m: 2.0%), i.e.
the test rejects a small fixed population of genuinely wrong candidates
(crossing roads) rather than trimming a continuum.
Applies only to parent edges the vertex rule did not match (8.0% of
741,889 Thai parent edges). Distance from such an edge's midpoint to
the nearest OSM way, 20,000 sampled: median 1.57 m, and
So the road is in OSM essentially always; the residual is the ~1.5 year
lag moving node positions, not missing geometry.
5 m rather than 10 m because a bearing test cannot protect against the
OPPOSITE CARRIAGEWAY of a divided road: it runs parallel, so its
bearing difference is ~0 and only distance separates it. Typical
carriageway spacing starts around 10 m, so 10 m would start attributing
a segment to the wrong side. The 14.7% of residual edges beyond 5 m
keep the honest 'unmatched' label instead of a guess.
Reads as: OSM accounts for at least 95% of this row's length.
Insensitive by design -- row coverage is concentrated at 1.0 (Thailand p5
is already 1.0), so the high share moves only from 98.9% at t=0.5 to 96.7%
at t=0.99. Thailand 97.3% / Maharashtra 96.1% at 0.95.
The column is therefore near-constant, so it carries little discriminating
power in safety_score._confidence_level (weight 0.15). It is accurate, and
it is less informative; both are true and the second is not a reason to
fake the first.
Kept two-valued: _confidence_level's cut points are calibrated for exactly
three two-valued columns.
Share of a row's MATCHED length whose ways are divided. Unmatched length
is excluded from the denominator: it is neither agreement nor dissent, and
osm_match_unmatched_frac reports it separately.
Also insensitive: the distribution is bimodal, not continuous. Of matched
Thai rows 63.7% are purely divided and 31.1% purely not, leaving 5.2%
strictly mixed (Maharashtra 25.2 / 65.8 / 9.0). is_divided therefore moves
only from 31,128 rows at t=0.5 to 29,132 at t=1.0 in Thailand.
0.95 rather than 1.0 so a single re-digitised sliver cannot veto a whole
divided highway, while still
requiring the evidence to cover the row, per the safety-side asymmetry
(raising V_safe needs evidence; leaving it at 30 km/h needs none).
